title: Magnetic Coupling
model_title: Magnetic (Synchronous Permanent-Magnet) Coupling with Containment Shell

introduction.definition: A magnetic coupling transmits torque without contact. Permanent magnets on an outer rotor attract opposite poles on an inner rotor through a thin containment shell, so the load side is hermetically sealed — no dynamic shaft seal is needed.
introduction.summary: A magnetic coupling transmits torque through a sealed wall without any shaft seal. Permanent magnets on an outer rotor (on the motor shaft) attract the opposite poles of magnets on an inner rotor (on the pump or mixer shaft). A thin, non-magnetic containment shell separates the two, so the process fluid is completely sealed — ideal for toxic, flammable or valuable liquids.

foundation: Mount driver and driven machines on a rigid common base so centre distances and alignment stay fixed.
alignment: Centre the outer rotor around the shell with the specified radial clearance; magnetic forces are strong — use assembly fixtures.
piping: Fit guards that fully enclose moving parts but allow inspection and lubrication.
commissioning: Check rotation, set tension/slack or torque setting, run in and re-check after the first hours of operation.

periodic.task: Check for rubbing marks on the shell.

lubrication: Grease for motor-side bearings; process-lubricated inner bearings on mag-drive pumps.

video_tutorials.title: Magnetic Coupling — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Magnetic Coupling.
A magnetic coupling transmits torque without contact.
Permanent magnets on an outer rotor attract opposite poles on an inner rotor through a thin containment shell, so the load side is hermetically sealed — no dynamic shaft seal is needed.
Typical applications include sealless (mag-drive) pumps for toxic/flammable liquids; mixers and reactors; vacuum and pressurised equipment; food and pharma (hygienic).

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Outer (Driving) Magnet Rotor on Motor Shaft — alternating N/S magnets, Containment Shell (Can) — static seal between atmosphere and process, Inner (Driven) Magnet Rotor on Pump/Load Shaft.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Magnetic Coupling.
Monitor bearing temperature and vibration.
Check for rubbing marks on the shell.
Replace bearings; check magnet strength.
Watch for decoupling: motor runs, load stopped. Common cause: overload, high viscosity, magnet overheating.
Watch for shell rupture: leak. Common cause: rubbing from bearing wear, overheating.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
